panels.rationale: Single-panel panoramic radiograph from a case report titled 'Stafne bone cavity containing ectopic parotid gland.' The caption describes an oval, well-bordered cystic radiolucency between the second molar and the mandibular angle, slightly above the inferior mandibular line, with denser surrounding borders — the classic radiographic appearance of a Stafne bone cavity (static bone cavity) in the posterior mandible. No expansion or root involvement, consistent with this entity. No skin or ethnicity data given; age not stated in caption or in-text.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows a panoramic radiograph demonstrating a classic radiolucent lesion near the mandibular canal, consistent with a Stafne's bone cavity. B: Panel B shows an axial CT demonstrating the typical involvement of both lingual and buccal plates in the defect, characteristic of Stafne Bone Cavity. C: Panel C shows a 3D reconstruction of the CT, confirming the tunnel-type lesion through complete discontinuity of both plates. D: Panel D is an MRI demonstrating soft tissue within the defect, which is contiguous to the submandibular gland, helping to characterize the mass inside the bony cavity.

in_text_mentions: In the panoramic radiography, a unilocular, ovoid, radiolucid, well-defined lesion, measuring approximately 0.6 cm x 0.9 cm, was located near the left mandibular angle below the mandibular canal (Fig. 1). No previous radiological exams were available.

In order to reveal the exact location of the defect, a computed tomography (CT) of the mandible was performed. Axial sections showed a defect, with discontinuity of the lingual plate, as well as, a significant erosion of the buccal cortex (Fig. 1). The 3D-reconstruction showed a tunnel-like lesion with a complete loss of continuity of both lingual and buccal plates (Fig. 1). Due to this last finding, a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in order to discard submandibular gland pathology (Fig. 1).
